summary: The MATCH Act requires federal agencies to place strict export controls on advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment, components, and related services to prevent countries of concern and specific foreign companies from acquiring foundational technology that supports advanced computing and military modernization. The bill directs federal officials to engage diplomatically with allied supplier countries to urge them to adopt aligned export restrictions and license requirements. If allies fail to adopt matching controls, the United States must independently enforce broader jurisdiction, end-use restrictions, and licensing rules with a policy of denial on equipment and servicing destined for covered facilities in countries of concern.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with new export restrictions, licensing requirements, and servicing prohibitions related to advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment destined for countries of concern.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Semiconductor Equipment Manufacturers and Exporters

affected_groups.effect: Face comprehensive export controls, license denials, and restrictions on receiving or servicing advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment and U.S.-origin technology.
affected_groups.group: Entities in Countries of Concern (including China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, and Russia)

key_provisions: Requires covered agency heads to identify and report on covered semiconductor manufacturing equipment and facilities within 60 days of enactment.
Mandates immediate diplomatic engagement with allied supplier countries to secure aligned countrywide export controls and licensing policies of denial.
Requires federal agencies to publish regulations establishing comprehensive U.S. restrictions and applying countrywide controls to covered equipment within 150 days.
Authorizes a one-time national security waiver of up to 90 days to extend the implementation deadline if allied countries are taking concrete, verifiable steps to adopt aligned controls.
Establishes a sunset provision terminating the Act five years after the date of enactment.

summary_detail.significance: The bill addresses national security concerns regarding advanced computing and military-civil fusion by seeking to block access by foreign adversaries to critical semiconductor technology. It creates statutory mandates for export controls and diplomatic alignment with international allies, carrying a significance score of 75.
